easy.def: A small, rough hut.
examples: The shack is old.
We found a shack in the woods.
The shack had one room.

more.def: A small, simple building that is roughly made.
examples: A fisherman lived in a tiny shack beside the lake.
The fishing shack stood on the ice.
The old shack leaned to one side.

easy.def: A cool, dark place away from the sun.
examples: We sat in the shade.
The shade is cool.
The tree gives shade.

more.def: An area that is darker and cooler because something blocks the sun.
examples: We sat in the shade of a big tree.
The shade was cool on the hot day.
The dog lay in the shade.

easy.def: A cover for a lamp or window.
examples: The lamp has a shade.
Pull down the shade.
The shade is blue.

more.def: A cover that is used to block or soften light, for a lamp or window.
examples: The lamp had a yellow shade.
She pulled the shade down to keep out the sun.
The window shade rolled up.

easy.def: A dark shape made when something blocks the light.
examples: I can see my shadow on the wall.
My shadow is long in the evening.
The cat jumped at its own shadow.

more.def: A dark shape that forms when something blocks light.
examples: In the evening, the trees cast long shadows across the lawn.
The tall building cast a shadow over the park.
We made shadow animals on the wall with our hands.

easy.def: A long, narrow hole going down.
examples: The elevator shaft is dark.
The mine has a deep shaft.
A shaft of light came in.

more.def: A long, narrow space going up or down, or a long thin beam of light.
examples: The elevator shaft was dark.
The miners went down the shaft.
A shaft of light came through the window.

easy.def: Having long, messy hair or fur.
examples: The dog is shaggy.
A shaggy rug is on the floor.
He has shaggy hair.

more.def: Covered in long, rough, untidy hair or fur.
examples: Our shaggy dog needs a haircut.
The yak's shaggy fur keeps it warm in the cold mountains.
A shaggy rug covered the floor of the cozy room.

easy.def: To move quickly up and down or side to side.
examples: Shake the bottle.
The dog shakes water off.
Leaves shake in the wind.

more.def: To move back and forth or up and down with quick, short movements.
examples: Shake the bottle before you pour.
The wet dog shook itself dry.
The ground shook when the train passed.

easy.def: A word used to offer or to ask a polite question.
examples: Shall we go?
Shall I help you?
We shall see.

more.def: A word used to make an offer or a suggestion, or to say what will happen.
examples: Shall I carry that heavy bag for you?
Shall we have lunch in the garden today?
We shall return before the sun goes down.

easy.def: Not deep.
examples: The pond is shallow.
A shallow dish.
The water is shallow here.

more.def: Not deep, with only a short distance from the top to the bottom.
examples: The pond is shallow, so we can wade.
I put the soup in a shallow bowl.
The water at the beach is shallow.

easy.def: A bad feeling about something you did.
examples: He felt shame.
She hung her head in shame.
The shame went away.

more.def: A painful feeling of being embarrassed or sorry about something you did.
examples: He felt shame when he told a lie.
A feeling of shame kept him quiet.
The shame faded after he said sorry.

easy.def: Something sad.
examples: It's a shame it rained.
What a shame!
It is a shame you cannot come.

more.def: A sad thing, or something to feel sorry about.
examples: It is a shame that it rained on the day of the picnic.
What a shame that you cannot come.
It would be a shame to waste the cake.

easy.def: Soap that you use to wash your hair.
examples: I use shampoo in the bath.
The shampoo smells like apples.
Mom bought a new bottle of shampoo.

more.def: A liquid soap used for washing hair and sometimes for cleaning rugs and car seats.
examples: Just a small amount of shampoo makes a lot of bubbles.
The dog's shampoo is made to be gentle on skin.
He read the label on the shampoo bottle to find out how to use it.

easy.def: To wash with soap made for hair.
examples: I shampoo my hair each night.
Dad will shampoo the dog today.
She shampooed her hair twice.

more.def: To wash hair or a rug with a special liquid soap.
examples: He shampooed the carpet to get out the muddy marks.
I shampooed my hair and rinsed it well.
The groomer shampooed the poodle before cutting its fur.

easy.def: What something looks like around its edges.
examples: A circle is a shape.
The cloud has a funny shape.
What shape is the cookie?

more.def: The form or outline of something.
examples: A star is a shape with points.
The cloud had the shape of a rabbit.
The cookies came in the shape of stars.

related.def: To give a new shape to something.

easy.def: To let others use or have part of what you have.
examples: I share my toys.
We shared the pizza.
Please share the crayons.

more.def: To let someone else use or have a part of something.
examples: The twins share a bedroom.
She shared her sandwich with a friend.
We share the swings at recess.

easy.def: A part of something.
examples: I ate my share.
Everyone got a share.
Each person gets a share.

more.def: A part of something that is given to or owned by one person.
examples: Each child got an equal share of the pie.
She did her share of the work.
My share of the money was five dollars.

easy.def: A big fish with sharp teeth.
examples: A shark swam by.
The shark has a big fin.
Sharks live in the sea.

more.def: A large sea fish with a strong body, a pointed fin and many sharp teeth.
examples: The shark swam past the divers.
Sharks have been in the ocean for millions of years.
The whale shark is the biggest fish in the sea.

easy.def: Able to cut well.
examples: The knife is sharp.
Be careful with the sharp scissors.
A cactus has sharp spines.

more.def: Having a thin edge or point that can cut or poke easily.
examples: The sharp knife cut the bread easily.
Be careful of the sharp thorns on the rose bush.
She sharpened the pencil to a sharp point.

easy.def: To break into many pieces.
examples: The glass will shatter.
The window shattered.
The vase shattered.

more.def: To break suddenly into many small pieces.
examples: The glass shattered on the floor.
The ball shattered the window.
The ice shattered when it hit the ground.

easy.def: To cut hair off close to the skin.
examples: Dad shaves his face.
The barber shaved his head.
The farmer shaved the sheep.

more.def: To cut hair off close to the skin with a sharp blade.
examples: Dad shaves his beard every morning.
The farmers shave the wool off the sheep in spring.
The barber shaved the back of his neck.

easy.def: A word for a girl or a woman.
examples: She is my sister.
She likes to paint.
Grandma said she is tired.

more.def: A word used for a girl, a woman, or a female animal that has already been talked about.
examples: My aunt is a pilot, and she flies to Japan every month.
The hen sat on her nest because she was guarding the eggs.
Maya practiced the piano until she could play the song.

easy.def: A small building for storing things.
examples: The tools are in the shed.
The shed is in the yard.
The bike is in the shed.

more.def: A small, simple building used for storing tools or other things.
examples: Dad keeps the lawn mower in the shed.
The shed at the back of the garden has a blue door.
We stored the firewood in a wooden shed.

easy.def: To lose hair, skin or leaves.
examples: The dog sheds in spring.
Trees shed their leaves.
The snake shed its skin.

more.def: To let something fall off, such as hair, skin or leaves.
examples: Our dog sheds hair all over the couch.
Trees shed their leaves in autumn.
The snake shed its old skin.

easy.def: A farm animal with a thick, woolly coat.
examples: The sheep eat grass.
Wool comes from a sheep.
The sheep said baa.

more.def: A farm animal with a thick coat of wool that is raised for wool and meat.
examples: The farmer sheared the sheep in spring.
A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
Wool for my sweater came from a sheep.

easy.def: Complete and total, with nothing else mixed in.
examples: It was sheer luck that we won.
I cried with sheer joy.
The sheer size of it amazed us.

more.def: Nothing more or less than; complete.
examples: We won by sheer luck and not because of skill.
She jumped for joy with sheer delight.
The sheer size of the whale left us speechless.

easy.def: Very thin, so you can see through it.
examples: The curtain is sheer.
She wore a sheer scarf.
The cloth is sheer.

more.def: Very thin and light, so that you can see through it.
examples: A sheer curtain let the morning light into the room.
She wore a sheer scarf over her hair.
The fabric was so sheer that you could read through it.

easy.def: Going almost straight up or down.
examples: The cliff was sheer.
A sheer wall of rock stood before us.
The sheer drop was scary.

more.def: Rising or falling in an almost straight line, with a very steep side.
examples: The climbers faced a sheer wall of rock.
A sheer cliff dropped down to the sea.
The mountain had a sheer drop of a thousand feet.

easy.def: A large cover that goes on a bed.
examples: Put the sheet on the bed.
The sheet is clean.
I pulled up the sheet.

more.def: A large piece of thin cloth that you lie on or under in a bed.
examples: Mom put clean sheets on the bed.
The kids made a tent from a sheet.
He pulled the sheet up to his chin.

easy.def: A thin, flat piece of paper or other material.
examples: Take a sheet of paper.
A sheet of ice covered the pond.
I need one more sheet.

more.def: A thin, flat, wide piece of something such as paper, metal or ice.
examples: Hand me a sheet of paper, please.
A sheet of ice covered the puddle.
Cookies bake on a flat metal sheet.

easy.def: A flat board on a wall for holding things.
examples: The books are on the shelf.
The shelf is high.
I put the toy on the shelf.

more.def: A flat board fixed to a wall or in a cupboard for holding things.
examples: The books are on the top shelf.
She put the vase on a shelf.
The shelf was too high to reach.

easy.def: The hard outside part of an egg or a nut.
examples: I found a shell on the beach.
The turtle has a hard shell.
The snail went into its shell.

more.def: The hard outer covering of an egg, a nut, or an animal such as a snail or turtle.
examples: I picked up a pretty shell on the beach.
The turtle pulled its head into its shell.
She cracked the shell of the egg.

easy.def: A safe place to stay.
examples: We found shelter from the rain.
The cat found shelter under the porch.
The bus stop is a shelter from the wind.

more.def: A place that covers and protects people or animals from weather or danger.
examples: The hikers built a shelter out of branches before the storm.
The barn gave the cows shelter from the snow.
People who lost their homes stayed at a shelter.

easy.def: A person who takes care of sheep.
examples: The shepherd watched the sheep.
A shepherd has a staff.
The shepherd called his dog.

more.def: A person whose job is to look after a flock of sheep.
examples: The shepherd watched the flock on the hill.
A shepherd sleeps near the sheep at night.
The shepherd whistled to his dog.

easy.def: The main police officer of a county.
examples: The sheriff wore a badge.
The sheriff helped us.
The sheriff rode a horse.

more.def: An elected officer who keeps order and enforces the law in a county.
examples: The sheriff drove through town.
In old stories, the sheriff wears a star badge.
The sheriff helped find the lost hikers.

easy.def: A sound you make to tell someone to be quiet.

more.def: A word used to tell someone to be quiet.
examples: Shh, the movie is about to start.
Shh, you will wake the baby with all that noise.
She put a finger to her lips and whispered, Shh, he's coming!

easy.def: Something that protects you.
examples: The knight held a shield.
A shield protects you.
The shield is round.

more.def: A large flat piece that a fighter holds to protect the body, or anything that protects.
examples: The knight raised his shield.
She wore a face shield for safety.
Clouds can shield the sun's heat.

easy.def: To keep someone safe.
examples: She shielded her eyes.
The umbrella shields me from the rain.
He shielded the baby from the wind.

more.def: To protect someone or something from harm.
examples: He shielded his eyes from the bright sun.
The umbrella shielded us from the rain.
She shielded the candle from the wind.

easy.def: To move a little.
examples: Shift your seat.
She shifted her weight.
The sand shifted.

more.def: To move something from one position to another.
examples: Shift your chair closer to the table.
She shifted her heavy bag to the other shoulder.
The wind shifted and blew from the north.

easy.def: A set work time.
examples: Dad works the night shift.
Her shift ends at five.
He started his shift.

more.def: A period of time during which a person works.
examples: Dad works the night shift at the hospital.
Her shift at the store ends at five.
The workers on the day shift went home.

easy.def: To give off light.
examples: The sun shines.
The stars shine at night.
Shine the flashlight here.

more.def: To give off a bright light, or to look bright because of light.
examples: The moon shone brightly over the lake.
The floor shines after Mom washes it.
He shined his shoes until they sparkled.

easy.def: Bright and sparkling.
examples: The shining sun is warm.
A shining star.
The shining car looked new.

more.def: Giving off light, or looking bright and polished.
examples: The shining sun warmed the beach.
A shining star appeared over the barn.
The shining floor reflected the lights.

easy.def: Bright and smooth.
examples: The new coin is shiny.
My shoes are shiny.
The shiny car looked clean.

more.def: Giving off light because it is smooth and polished.
examples: The shiny coin sparkled in the sun.
He polished his shoes until they were shiny.
The new car was bright and shiny.

easy.def: A very big boat.
examples: The ship sailed across the sea.
We saw a ship at the port.
The ship carried cars.

more.def: A large boat that carries people or goods across the sea.
examples: The ship sailed across the ocean for a week.
Cargo ships bring toys from faraway factories.
Dolphins swam alongside the ship.

easy.def: To send something far away.
examples: Please ship the package.
They ship toys by train.
We shipped it to Grandma.

more.def: To send goods from one place to another, often by truck, train or boat.
examples: The company ships apples to stores all over the country.
We shipped a box of cookies to my cousin.
Farmers ship their corn by train.

easy.def: Goods sent to a place.
examples: The shipment arrived.
A shipment of toys came.
The shipment is late.

more.def: A load of goods that is sent from one place to another.
examples: A shipment of toys arrived at the store.
The shipment was late because of the storm.
The farmer sent a shipment of apples.

easy.def: Clothing for the top of your body.
examples: Put on a shirt.
My shirt is red.
He wore a clean shirt.

more.def: A piece of clothing that covers the upper body, usually with sleeves.
examples: She wore a striped shirt to school.
He spilled juice on his shirt.
Tuck your shirt in.

related.def: A shirt worn under another shirt.

easy.def: To shake because you are cold or scared.

more.def: To shake slightly because you are cold or frightened.
examples: We shivered at the bus stop in the icy wind.

easy.def: A big surprise.

more.def: A sudden, big surprise that is upsetting.
examples: It was a shock to see the house empty.
The loud noise gave me a shock.

easy.def: To surprise someone a lot.
examples: The noise shocked me.
The news shocked us.
She shocked the class.

more.def: To surprise and upset someone.
examples: The loud crash shocked everyone.
The news shocked the whole town.
His quick answer shocked the teacher.

easy.def: Very surprising and upsetting.
examples: The news was shocking.
A shocking sight.
It was shocking to see.

more.def: Causing a sudden, strong feeling of surprise and upset.
examples: The news was shocking, and we gasped.
The messy room was a shocking sight.

easy.def: Something you wear on your foot.
examples: Tie your shoe.

My shoes are muddy.

more.def: A covering for the foot, usually with a hard bottom and a place for laces.
examples: She tied her shoe and ran outside.
A pebble got into my shoe.

easy.def: To kick or throw a ball at a goal.
examples: She shoots the ball.

more.def: To throw or kick a ball toward a goal or basket in a game.

easy.def: To take a picture or a movie.

more.def: To take a photograph or film a movie.

easy.def: To send an arrow out fast with a bow.

more.def: To send an arrow or another object out fast from a bow or a launcher.
examples: At camp, we learned how to shoot arrows at a target.

easy.def: A small store.
examples: The shop sells toys.

more.def: A small store that sells certain things.
examples: The bakery is the best shop on our street.

easy.def: To go to stores to buy things.
examples: We shop for food.

more.def: To go to shops or stores to look at and buy things.
examples: We shop for groceries every Friday.
She shopped for a birthday gift for her brother.

easy.def: Going to stores to buy things.
examples: We go shopping.
Shopping is fun.
Mom does the shopping.

more.def: The act of going to stores to look at and buy things.
examples: We went shopping for new shoes.
Mom does the grocery shopping on Saturdays.
Holiday shopping can be busy.

easy.def: Not long.
examples: The rope is short.

She has short hair.

more.def: Not long in length or time.
examples: We took a short walk after dinner.
The kitten's tail is short.
It was a short movie.

easy.def: Not tall.
examples: He is short.

My brother is short.

more.def: Not tall; low in height.
examples: She is short, but she can jump high.

more.def: Having less than you need.

more.def: A way that is shorter or faster than the usual one.

easy.def: Soon.

more.def: In a short time from now.

easy.def: Short pants that end above the knee.

My shorts are blue.
The shorts are comfy.

more.def: Pants that end above the knees.
examples: I wear shorts when it is hot.
He changed into swim shorts.
The soccer shorts are blue.

easy.def: A needle that puts medicine in your arm.

more.def: A small amount of medicine put into the body with a needle, to keep you from getting sick.
examples: I got a flu shot at the doctor's office.

easy.def: A try to hit or score in a game.

What a good shot!

more.def: An attempt to hit, kick, or throw a ball toward a goal.
examples: She took a shot and the ball went into the net.

easy.def: The part of the body between your neck and arm.

more.def: The place where the arm joins the body, below the neck.

easy.def: To say something very loudly.

more.def: To say something in a very loud voice.

easy.def: To push someone or something hard.

more.def: To push something hard, often in a rough way.

easy.def: A tool for digging.

more.def: To move snow or dirt using a wide, flat tool on a long handle.

easy.def: To let someone see something.

easy.def: Something to watch on a stage or TV.

more.def: A performance or program that people watch, such as on a stage or on TV.

more.def: A way of washing in which water sprays down from above.

easy.def: A short rain.

more.def: A short fall of rain.

more.def: To cut or tear something into long, thin pieces.

easy.def: High and sharp in sound.

easy.def: A small sea animal with a curved body that people eat.

more.def: A small sea animal with a thin shell and a bent body that is eaten as food.
examples: We had shrimp for dinner.

easy.def: To get smaller.

more.def: To become smaller in size or amount.

more.def: A bus, train or plane that travels back and forth over a short distance.

more.def: Nervous or uncomfortable around people you do not know well.
